title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 24 (Power of SEBI to Regulate Issue and Transfer of Securities, etc.)

content.overview: Section 24 allocates regulatory power: SEBI administers specified matters relating to issue and transfer of securities and non-payment of dividend for listed companies and companies intending to list; the Central Government retains residual administration.
content.glance: State SEBI’s allocated field; note Central Government residual role; link to s. 23 issue routes.
content.study: Section 24 is a regulatory-allocation provision. Matters relating to issue and transfer of securities and non-payment of dividend under the relevant Chapters are administered by SEBI for listed companies and companies intending to list. In other cases those matters are administered by the Central Government. SEBI may call for information, inspect, inquire, investigate and levy penalties in its allocated field. Current-law framing: identify listing status or intention to list; assign the regulator; then apply substantive rules.

sections.heading: SEBI’s Allocated Field
sections.body: Issue and transfer of securities and non-payment of dividend for listed companies and companies intending to list are administered by SEBI.

sections.heading: Central Government Residual Role
sections.body: Matters outside SEBI’s allocated field remain with the Central Government.

sections.heading: SEBI’s Powers
sections.body: SEBI may call for information, inspect, inquire, investigate and levy penalties in respect of allocated matters.

sections.heading: Application Test
sections.body: Determine listing status; assign administrator; apply substantive Companies Act and SEBI rules.

provisions.title: Power of Securities and Exchange Board to regulate issue and transfer of securities, etc.

examples.title: Listed company dividend default
examples.body: A listed company fails to pay declared dividend. Under s. 24 the matter is administered by SEBI.

examples.title: Unlisted private placement
examples.body: An unlisted private company makes a private placement. SEBI’s s. 24 field is not engaged by listing.

hypotheticals.question: Does SEBI administer every securities issue under the Companies Act?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 24 allocates specified matters for listed/intending-to-list companies; other cases remain with the Central Government.

misconceptions.trap: SEBI replaces the Companies Act for all companies.
misconceptions.correction: Section 24 allocates administration of specified matters; it does not repeal the Companies Act.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 24 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Determine listing status. II. Identify the matter. III. Assign SEBI or CG. IV. Apply substance. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Listing status; allocated matter; administrator; precise relief.

examTips: Test listing or intention to list first.
Do not treat s. 24 as a complete securities code.
